title.zh: 卷二十二 列傳第十六 太祖五王
title.raw: 卷二十二 列傳第十六 太祖五王 Volume 22: Five Princes of Taizu

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第二十二 列傳第十六

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 22, Biographies 16
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 22, Biographies 16

sentences.zh: 太祖五王

translations.literal: The Five Princes of Taizu
translations.idiomatic: The Five Princes of Taizu

sentences.zh: 太祖十男。

translations.literal: Taizu had ten sons.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor had ten sons.

sentences.zh: 張皇后生長沙宣武王懿、永陽昭王敷、高祖、衡陽宣王暢。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang bore Prince Xuanwu of Changsha Yi, Prince Zhao of Yongyang Fu, the High Ancestor, and Prince Xuan of Hengyang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang was the mother of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi; Prince Zhao of Yongyang, Fu; the future Emperor Wu; and Prince Xuan of Hengyang, Chang.

sentences.zh: 李太妃生桂陽簡王融。

translations.literal: Consort Li bore Prince Jian of Guiyang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li gave birth to Prince Jian of Guiyang, Rong.

sentences.zh: 懿及融，齊永元中爲東昏所害；

translations.literal: Yi and Rong, in the Yongyuan era of Qi, were killed by Donghun;
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Rong were put to death by Emperor Donghun of Qi during the Yongyuan era;

sentences.zh: 敷、暢，建武中卒：高祖踐阼，並追封郡王。

translations.literal: Fu and Chang died in the Jianwu era: when the High Ancestor ascended the throne, all were posthumously enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Chang died during the Jianwu era. When Emperor Wu took the throne, all four were posthumously created princes of their respective commanderies.

sentences.zh: 陳太妃生臨川靖惠王宏，南平元襄王偉。

translations.literal: Consort Chen bore Prince Jinghui of Linchuan Hong and Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Chen was the mother of Prince Jinghui of Linchuan, Hong, and Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping, Wei.

sentences.zh: 吳太妃生安成康王秀，始興忠武王憺。

translations.literal: Consort Wu bore Prince Kang of Ancheng Xiu and Prince Zhongwu of Shixing Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu gave birth to Prince Kang of Ancheng, Xiu, and Prince Zhongwu of Shixing, Dan.

sentences.zh: 費太妃生鄱陽忠烈王恢。

translations.literal: Consort Fei bore Prince Zhonglie of Poyang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Fei was the mother of Prince Zhonglie of Poyang, Hui.

sentences.zh: 臨川靖惠王宏字宣達，太祖第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jinghui of Linchuan Hong, styled Xuanda, was the sixth son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jinghui of Linchuan, Hong, whose style was Xuanda, was the founding emperor's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 長八尺，美鬚眉，容止可觀。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi tall, with handsome brows and beard, and bearing that invited regard.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi in height, with handsome features and a beard, and carried himself in a manner that drew admiration.

sentences.zh: 齊永明十年，爲衛軍廬陵王法曹行參軍，遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming of Qi, he became Acting Army Aide of the Legal Bureau under the Prince of Luling in the Guard General's command, and was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Yongming reign of Qi, he served as acting aide in the legal bureau of the Prince of Luling under the Guard General, and was later promoted to attendant of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時長沙王懿鎮梁州，爲魏所圍，明年，給宏精兵千人赴援，未至，魏軍退。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Changsha Yi was stationed at Liang Province and was besieged by Wei; the next year Hong was given a thousand elite troops to go to his relief, but before they arrived the Wei army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Changsha, Yi, was defending Liang Province and came under siege by Northern Wei. The following year Hong was dispatched with a thousand picked troops to relieve him, but before they arrived the Wei forces had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎晉安王主簿，尋爲北中郎桂陽王功曹史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Jin'an under the Flying Cavalry General, and soon became Recorder of the Merit Bureau for the Prince of Guiyang under the Northern Central Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed chief clerk to the Prince of Jin'an under the Flying Cavalry General, and soon afterward became recorder in the merit bureau of the Prince of Guiyang under the Northern Central Commander.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王暢，有美名，爲始安王蕭遙光所禮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hengyang Chang had a fine reputation and was treated with honor by the Prince of Shi'an Xiao Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hengyang, Chang, enjoyed a fine reputation and was treated with great respect by Prince Shi'an, Xiao Yaoguang.

sentences.zh: 及遙光作亂，逼暢入東府，暢懼禍，先赴臺。

translations.literal: When Yaoguang rebelled, he forced Chang into the Eastern Palace; Chang, fearing disaster, went first to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoguang rose in rebellion, he compelled Chang to enter the Eastern Palace. Fearing for his life, Chang went to the imperial capital ahead of the others.

sentences.zh: 高祖在雍州，常懼諸弟及禍，謂南平王偉曰：「六弟明於事理，必先還臺。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was in Yong Province and often feared his younger brothers would meet with disaster; he said to the Prince of Nanping Wei: "The sixth brother understands affairs clearly and will surely return to the capital first.
translations.idiomatic: While still in Yong Province, the future Emperor Wu often worried that his younger brothers would be caught up in the turmoil. He told Prince Nanping, Wei, "Our sixth brother has a clear head for affairs; he will be the first to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」及信至，果如高祖策。

translations.literal: " When the news arrived, it was indeed as the High Ancestor had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: " When word arrived, events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 高祖義師下，宏至新林奉迎，拜輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor's righteous army marched east, Hong went to Xinlin to welcome him and was appointed General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu's army marched east, Hong went to Xinlin to welcome him and was appointed General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 建康平，遷西中郎將、中護軍，領石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, he was transferred to General of the Western Central Commandant, Central Protector of the Army, and took charge of military affairs at the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiankang was secured, he was promoted to general of the western central commandant and central protector of the army, with responsibility for the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，封臨川郡王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian, he was created Prince of Linchuan with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督揚、南徐州諸軍事、後將軍、揚州刺史，又給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Soon he became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yang and Southern Xuzhou, Rear General, and Governor of Yang Province, and was also granted a set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made bearer of the staff of authority, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yang and southern Xuzhou, rear general, and governor of Yang Province, and was also granted a full set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 三年，加侍中，進號中軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional title Palace Attendant and advanced in rank to General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was additionally appointed palace attendant and promoted to general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖詔北伐，以宏爲都督南北兗北徐青冀豫司霍八州北討諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the High Ancestor ordered a northern campaign and made Hong Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition over the eight provinces of Southern and Northern Yan, Northern Xu, Qing, Ji, Yu, Si, and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Wu ordered a northern expedition and appointed Hong commander of the northern campaign over the eight provinces of southern and northern Yan, northern Xu, Qing, Ji, Yu, Si, and Huo.

sentences.zh: 宏以帝之介弟，所領皆器械精新，軍容甚盛，北人以爲百數十年所未之有。

translations.literal: Hong, as the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, led troops whose weapons were all finely made and new; his military appearance was very imposing, and the northerners considered it unmatched in more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's uterine younger brother, Hong commanded troops equipped with the finest new arms. His army's appearance was so magnificent that the northerners said they had seen nothing like it in more than a century.

sentences.zh: 軍次洛口，宏前軍剋梁城，斬魏將鼂清。

translations.literal: The army halted at Luokou; Hong's vanguard took Liangcheng and beheaded the Wei general Chao Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Luokou. Hong's vanguard captured Liangcheng and beheaded the Wei general Chao Qing.

sentences.zh: 會征役久，有詔班師。

translations.literal: As the campaign had dragged on, an edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Because the campaign had dragged on, an edict ordered the troops to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，遷驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he was transferred to Flying Cavalry General and given the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies with an open office, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he was promoted to flying cavalry general with the ceremonial privileges of the three excellencies and an open office, while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷司徒，領太子太傅。

translations.literal: That same year he was transferred to Minister of Education and concurrently served as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Later that year he was appointed minister of education and concurrently served as grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，爲使持節、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、司空、揚州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year he became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yang and Southern Xu, Minister of Works, and Governor of Yang Province, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year he was made bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Yang and southern Xu, minister of works, and governor of Yang Province, while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，以公事左遷驃騎大將軍，開府同三司之儀，侍中如故。

translations.literal: That winter, on account of public business he was demoted to the left as Grand General of the Flying Cavalry with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and an open office, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on account of official misconduct, he was demoted to grand general of the flying cavalry with ceremonial privileges equal to the three excellencies and an open office, while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遷使持節、都督揚徐二州諸軍事、揚州刺史，侍中、將軍如故。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yang and Xu, and Governor of Yang Province, with his posts as Palace Attendant and General unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the new title, he was reassigned as bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Yang and Xu, and governor of Yang Province, while retaining his posts as palace attendant and general.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷司空，使持節、侍中、都督、刺史、將軍並如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Minister of Works; his titles as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief, Governor, and General all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed minister of works, while his titles as bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander, governor, and general all remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十七年夏，以公事左遷侍中、中軍將軍、行司徒。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventeenth year, on account of public business he was demoted to the left as Palace Attendant, General of the Central Army, and Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventeenth year he was again demoted for official misconduct to palace attendant, general of the central army, and acting minister of education.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，遷侍中、中書監、司徒。

translations.literal: That winter he was transferred to Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed palace attendant, supervisor of the secretariat, and minister of education.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，遷使持節、都督揚、南徐州諸軍事、太尉、揚州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yang and Southern Xu, Grand Commandant, and Governor of Yang Province, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong he was made bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Yang and southern Xu, grand commandant, and governor of Yang Province, while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 二年，改創南、北郊，以本官領起部尚書，事竟罷。

translations.literal: In the second year the southern and northern suburban altars were rebuilt; with his existing offices he concurrently headed the Ministry for Initiating Works, and when the task was finished he was relieved of that duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the southern and northern suburban altars were rebuilt, he concurrently served as minister for initiating works in addition to his existing posts; when the project was completed, he relinquished that additional office.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，以疾累表自陳，詔許解揚州，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, on account of illness he repeatedly memorialized to resign; an edict permitted him to relinquish Yang Province while his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he repeatedly submitted memorials asking to resign on account of illness. An edict allowed him to step down as governor of Yang Province while his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四月，薨，時年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he died, at the age of fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he died, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 自疾至於薨，輿駕七出臨視。

translations.literal: From his illness until his death, the imperial carriage went out seven times to visit him in person.
translations.idiomatic: From the onset of his illness until his death, the emperor personally visited him seven times.

sentences.zh: 及葬，詔曰：「侍中、太尉臨川王宏，器宇沖貴，雅量弘通。

translations.literal: At his burial an edict said: "Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, Prince of Linchuan Hong—his bearing was serene and noble, his generous measure broad and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his burial an edict declared: "Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, Prince of Linchuan, Hong, possessed a serene and noble bearing and a broad, penetrating magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 爰初弱齡，行彰素履；

translations.literal: From his earliest youth his conduct displayed his plain integrity;
translations.idiomatic: From his earliest youth his conduct displayed unadorned integrity;

sentences.zh: 逮于應務，嘉猷載緝。

translations.literal: when he took up affairs of state, fine plans were continually brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: and once he took up affairs of state, fine plans were continually brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 自皇業啓基，地惟介弟，久司神甸，歷位臺階，論道登朝，物無異議。

translations.literal: Since the imperial enterprise was founded, as the emperor's uterine younger brother he long administered the sacred heartland, passed through the highest offices of state, and when he discoursed on the Way at court, no one voiced dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty was founded, as the emperor's uterine younger brother he had long administered the capital region, risen through the highest offices of state, and when he addressed policy at court, no one voiced dissent.

sentences.zh: 朕友于之至，家國兼情，方弘燮贊，儀刑列辟。

translations.literal: In the utmost of brotherly affection between Us, with feeling shared for family and state alike, We were about to extend his harmonizing support and make him a model for the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: In the deepest bonds of brotherhood between us, sharing affection for both family and realm, We had looked to extend his harmonizing counsel and make him a model for the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 天不憖遺，奄焉不永，哀痛抽切，震慟于厥心。

translations.literal: Heaven did not spare him; suddenly he was not long for this world—Our grief cuts to the quick and Our heart is shaken with anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven did not spare him; suddenly he was gone. Our grief cuts to the quick and Our heart is shaken with anguish.

sentences.zh: 宜增峻禮秩，式昭懋典。

translations.literal: His ceremonial rank should be raised in solemnity to display the full measure of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: His ceremonial rank should be raised in solemnity to display the full measure of his merit.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、大將軍、揚州牧、假黃鉞，王如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Grand General, Governor of Yang Province, and the provisional yellow battle-axe, with his princely title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted the titles of palace attendant, grand general, and governor of Yang Province, together with the provisional yellow battle-axe, while his princely title remains unchanged.

sentences.zh: 並給羽葆鼓吹一部，增班劍爲六十人。

translations.literal: He shall also be given a set of feathered parasols and martial music, and his guard of ceremonial swords increased to sixty men.
translations.idiomatic: He shall also be granted a set of feathered parasols and martial music, and his guard of ceremonial swords increased to sixty men.

sentences.zh: 給溫明秘器，斂以袞服。

translations.literal: The secret vessels of Wenming shall be provided, and he shall be laid in state in the dragon robes.
translations.idiomatic: The secret vessels of Wenming shall be provided, and he shall be laid in state in the dragon robes.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靖惠。

translations.literal: His posthumous title shall be Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title shall be Jinghui, "Serene and Gracious."

sentences.zh: 」宏性寬和篤厚，在州二十餘年，未嘗以吏事按郡縣，時稱其長者。

translations.literal: " Hong's nature was generous, harmonious, and sincere; during more than twenty years in the provinces he never used administrative matters to bring pressure on commanderies and counties, and at the time he was called a man of mature virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong was generous, harmonious, and sincere by nature. During more than twenty years in provincial office he never used administrative matters to bring pressure on the commanderies and counties under him, and at the time he was praised as a man of mature virtue.

sentences.zh: 宏有七子：正仁，正義，正德、正則，正立，正表，正信。

translations.literal: Hong had seven sons: Zhengren, Zhengyi, Zhengde, Zhengzhe, Zhengli, Zhengbiao, and Zhengxin.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had seven sons: Zhengren, Zhengyi, Zhengde, Zhengzhe, Zhengli, Zhengbiao, and Zhengxin.

sentences.zh: 世子正仁，爲吳興太守，有治能。

translations.literal: The heir Zhengren served as Governor of Wuxing and had ability in governance.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent, Zhengren, served as governor of Wuxing and proved capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 天監十年，卒，諡曰哀世子。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianjian he died; his posthumous title was Lamented Heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianjian he died, and was given the posthumous title Lamented Heir.

sentences.zh: 無子，高祖詔以羅平侯正立爲世子，由宏意也。

translations.literal: He had no son; the High Ancestor decreed that the Marquis of Luoping Zhengli should become heir, according to Hong's wish.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son. Emperor Wu decreed that the Marquis of Luoping, Zhengli, should succeed as heir, in accordance with Hong's own wish.

sentences.zh: 宏薨，正立表讓正義爲嗣，高祖嘉而許之，改封正立爲建安侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Hong died, Zhengli memorialized to yield the succession to Zhengyi; the High Ancestor commended this and approved it, and changed Zhengli's enfeoffment to Marquis of Jian'an with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong died, Zhengli submitted a memorial offering the succession to Zhengyi. Emperor Wu commended this and approved it, changing Zhengli's title to Marquis of Jian'an with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 卒，子賁嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Ben succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Ben succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 正義先封平樂侯，正德西豊侯，正則樂山侯，正立羅平侯，正表封山侯，正信武化侯，正德別有傳。

translations.literal: Zhengyi had earlier been enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingle; Zhengde as Marquis of Xifeng; Zhengzhe as Marquis of Leshan; Zhengli as Marquis of Luoping; Zhengbiao as Marquis of Fengshan; Zhengxin as Marquis of Wuhua; Zhengde has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyi had earlier been created Marquis of Pingle; Zhengde, Marquis of Xifeng; Zhengzhe, Marquis of Leshan; Zhengli, Marquis of Luoping; Zhengbiao, Marquis of Fengshan; and Zhengxin, Marquis of Wuhua. Zhengde is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 安成康王秀字彥達，太祖第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Kang of Ancheng Xiu, styled Yanda, was the seventh son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang of Ancheng, Xiu, whose style was Yanda, was the founding emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 年十二，所生母吳太妃亡，秀母弟始興王憺時年九歲，並以孝聞，居喪，累日不進漿飲，太祖親取粥授之。

translations.literal: At twelve his birth mother Consort Wu died; Xiu and his younger brother by the same mother, the Prince of Shixing Dan, then nine years old, were both famed for filial piety; in mourning they went many days without taking gruel, and Taizu personally brought porridge and fed them.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve his birth mother, Consort Wu, died. Xiu and his younger uterine brother, Prince Shixing, Dan, then nine years old, were both famed for filial devotion. During the mourning period they went many days without taking even gruel, until the founding emperor personally brought porridge and fed them.

sentences.zh: 哀其早孤，命側室陳氏並母二子。

translations.literal: Pitying their early orphanhood, he ordered the concubine Lady Chen to be mother to both sons together.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by their early loss, he ordered the concubine Lady Chen to serve as mother to both boys.

sentences.zh: 陳亦無子，有母德，視二子如親生焉。

translations.literal: Chen also had no children of her own but possessed the virtue of a mother and regarded the two sons as if they were her own.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen had no children of her own but possessed true maternal virtue, and she treated the two boys as if they were her own.

sentences.zh: 秀旣長，美風儀，性方靜，雖左右近侍，非正衣冠不見也，由是親友及家人咸敬焉。

translations.literal: When Xiu had grown up, he had fine bearing and dignity; his nature was upright and calm—even to close attendants at his side he would not appear unless properly dressed, and for this reason kin, friends, and household all held him in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult Xiu possessed fine bearing and dignity. His nature was upright and reserved—even close attendants at his side would not see him unless he was properly dressed. For this reason kin, friends, and household all held him in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 齊世，弱冠爲著作佐郎，累遷後軍法曹行參軍，太子舍人。

translations.literal: Under Qi, at his capping he became Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Army Aide of the Legal Bureau under the Rear General and Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi, upon reaching his capping age he became assistant gentleman of the secretariat, and was repeatedly promoted to acting aide in the legal bureau under the rear general and attendant of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 永元中，長沙宣武王懿入平崔慧景，爲尚書令，居端右；

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha Yi entered the capital to pacify Cui Huijing and became Director of the Masters of Writing, occupying the chief position on the right;
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongyuan era, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, entered the capital to suppress Cui Huijing and was appointed director of the masters of writing, occupying the chief position at court;

sentences.zh: 弟衡陽王暢爲衛尉，掌管籥。

translations.literal: his younger brother the Prince of Hengyang Chang was Commandant of the Guard and controlled the keys.
translations.idiomatic: while his younger brother Prince Hengyang, Chang, served as commandant of the guard and controlled the palace keys.

sentences.zh: 東昏日夕逸遊，出入無度。

translations.literal: Donghun day and night indulged in reckless roaming, coming and going without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun spent his days and nights in reckless roaming, coming and going without restraint.

sentences.zh: 衆頗勸懿因其出，閉門舉兵廢之，懿不聽。

translations.literal: Many urged Yi to take advantage of his going out, shut the gates, and raise troops to depose him, but Yi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Many urged Yi to seize the moment when the emperor went out, shut the gates, and raise troops to depose him, but Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 帝左右旣惡懿勳高，又慮廢立，並間懿，懿亦危之，自是諸王侯咸爲之備。

translations.literal: The emperor's close attendants already resented Yi's high merit and also feared deposition and enthronement; they all slandered Yi, and Yi too felt himself in peril—from this time all the princes and marquises took precautions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's close attendants already resented Yi's towering merit and also feared a coup to depose and replace him. They all slandered Yi, and Yi himself felt endangered. From that time all the princes and marquises took precautions.

sentences.zh: 及難作，臨川王宏以下諸弟侄各得奔避。

translations.literal: When the crisis broke out, the Prince of Linchuan Hong and the younger brothers and nephews below him each managed to flee and escape.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis broke out, Prince Linchuan, Hong, and the younger brothers and nephews below him each managed to flee to safety.

sentences.zh: 方其逃也，皆不出京師，而罕有發覺，惟桂陽王融及禍。

translations.literal: At the time of their flight none left the capital, yet few were discovered; only the Prince of Guiyang Rong met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Though none of them left the capital during their flight, few were discovered. Only Prince Guiyang, Rong, met with disaster.

sentences.zh: 六年，出爲使持節、都督江州諸軍事、平南將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Jiang Province, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was posted as bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Jiang Province, general who pacifies the south, and governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 將發，主者求堅船以爲齋舫。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the steward sought sturdy boats to serve as the vegetarian-ceremony vessel.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, his staff requested sturdy boats to serve as the ceremonial vessel for vegetarian offerings.

sentences.zh: 秀曰：「吾豈愛財而不愛士。

translations.literal: Xiu said: "How could I value wealth and not value gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "How could I value wealth and not value gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 」乃教所由，以牢者給參佐，下者載齋物。

translations.literal: " He then instructed those in charge to give the sturdiest boats to his staff officers and use the inferior ones to carry the ceremonial goods.
translations.idiomatic: " He then instructed his staff to assign the sturdiest boats to his officers and use the weaker ones to carry the ceremonial goods.

sentences.zh: 旣而遭風，齋舫遂破。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they encountered wind and the ceremonial vessel was wrecked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they encountered a storm, and the ceremonial vessel was wrecked.

sentences.zh: 及至州，聞前刺史取徵士陶潛曾孫爲里司。

translations.literal: When he reached the province, he heard that the previous governor had appointed a great-grandson of the recluse Tao Qian as village overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his province, he learned that the previous governor had appointed a great-grandson of the recluse Tao Qian as village overseer.

sentences.zh: 秀歎曰：「陶潛之德，豈可不及後世！

translations.literal: Xiu sighed and said: "The virtue of Tao Qian—how could it fail to reach later generations!
translations.idiomatic: Xiu sighed and said, "The virtue of Tao Qian—how could it fail to reach later generations!

sentences.zh: 」卽日辟爲西曹。

translations.literal: " That same day he summoned him to the Western Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he summoned the man to serve in the western bureau.

sentences.zh: 時盛夏水汎長，津梁斷絕，外司請依舊僦度，收其價直。

translations.literal: At that time in the height of summer the waters had risen and the ferry bridges were cut off; the outer offices requested that, according to precedent, ferry fees be collected.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of summer the rivers had swollen and the ferry crossings were cut off. The outer offices requested that ferry fees be collected according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 秀教曰：「刺史不德，水潦爲患，可利之乎！

translations.literal: Xiu instructed: "The governor lacks virtue, and floodwaters are the affliction—how could one profit from this!
translations.idiomatic: Xiu instructed them, "If the governor lacks virtue and floodwaters afflict the people, how can we profit from their distress!

sentences.zh: 給船而已。

translations.literal: Provide boats, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Provide boats, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」七年，遭慈母陳太妃憂，詔起視事。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year he suffered mourning for his beloved mother Consort Chen; an edict ordered him to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventh year he entered mourning for his beloved foster mother, Consort Chen. An edict ordered him to leave mourning and resume office.

sentences.zh: 尋遷都督荊湘雍益寧南北梁南北秦州九州諸軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the nine provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Ning, Southern and Northern Liang, Southern and Northern Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to commander of military affairs in the nine provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Ning, southern and northern Liang, and southern and northern Qin, with the title of general who pacifies the west and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷號安西將軍。

translations.literal: That year his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: That year his title was advanced to general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 立學校，招隱逸。

translations.literal: He established schools and recruited recluses.
translations.idiomatic: He established schools and recruited recluses and men of retirement.

sentences.zh: 下教曰：「夫鶉火之禽，不匿影於丹山；

translations.literal: He issued an instruction saying: "The bird of the Quail Fire constellation does not hide its shadow on the Crimson Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: He issued an instruction saying, "The bird of the Quail Fire constellation does not hide its shadow on the Crimson Mountain;

sentences.zh: 昭華之寶，乍耀采於藍田。

translations.literal: the treasure of Zhaohua suddenly flashes its splendor at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: the treasure of Zhaohua suddenly flashes its splendor at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 是以江漢有濯纓之歌，空谷著來思之詠，弘風闡道，靡不由茲。

translations.literal: Therefore along the Jiang and Han there is the song of washing the tassel; in the empty valley is recorded the ode of longing for the worthy—to spread the wind and expound the Way, nothing does not proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: Hence along the Jiang and Han came the song of washing the tassel clean, and in the empty valley arose the ode of longing for the worthy. To spread culture and expound the Way, nothing succeeds without such men.

sentences.zh: 處士河東韓懷明、南平韓望、南郡庾承先、河東郭麻，並脫落風塵，高蹈其事。

translations.literal: The recluses Han Huaiming of Hedong, Han Wang of Nanping, Yu Chengxian of Nan Commandery, and Guo Ma of Hedong all shook off the dust of the world and loftily pursued their calling.
translations.idiomatic: The recluses Han Huaiming of Hedong, Han Wang of Nanping, Yu Chengxian of Nan Commandery, and Guo Ma of Hedong had all shaken off the dust of the world and loftily pursued their calling.

sentences.zh: 兩韓之孝友純深，庾、郭之形骸枯槁，或橡飯菁羹，惟日不足，或葭牆艾席，樂在其中。

translations.literal: The two Hans' filial piety and brotherly affection were pure and deep; Yu and Guo's bodies were withered and gaunt—some ate acorn meal and wild-vegetable broth and found each day insufficient, others had reed walls and mugwort mats and took joy therein.
translations.idiomatic: The two Hans were renowned for pure and deep filial piety and brotherly affection; Yu and Guo had withered, gaunt frames. Some lived on acorn meal and wild-vegetable broth and still found each day insufficient; others dwelt behind reed walls on mugwort mats and took joy therein.

sentences.zh: 昔伯武貞堅，就仕河內，史雲孤劭，屈志陳留。

translations.literal: In former times Bo Wu was steadfast and took office in Henei; Shi Yun was solitary and strenuous and bent his will in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Bo Wu was steadfast and took office in Henei; Shi Yun was solitary and strenuous and bent his will to serve in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 豈曰場苗，實惟攻玉。

translations.literal: Was it not said to remove the overgrowth? In truth it is to polish jade.
translations.idiomatic: Was it not said that clearing the field is, in truth, polishing jade.

sentences.zh: 可加引辟，幷遣喻意。

translations.literal: They may be summoned and recommended, and envoys shall be sent to convey Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: They may be summoned and recommended, and envoys shall be sent to convey my intent.

sentences.zh: 旣同魏侯致禮之請，庶無辟昞彊三緘之歎。」

translations.literal: Thus it is the same as the Marquis of Wei's request to show ritual courtesy; may there be none of the thrice-sealed sigh of one who shuns the bright and forces silence."
translations.idiomatic: Thus it shall be as when the Marquis of Wei asked to show ritual courtesy, and may there be none of the thrice-sealed sigh of one who shuns the light and seals his lips in silence."

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏懸瓠城民反，殺豫州刺史司馬悅，引司州刺史馬仙琕，仙琕簽荊州求應赴。

translations.literal: That year the people of Xuanché in Wei rebelled, killed the Governor of Yu Province Sima Yue, and summoned the Governor of Si Province Ma Xianbi; Xianbi wrote to Jing Province requesting support to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: That year the people of Xuanché in Wei rebelled, killed the governor of Yu Province, Sima Yue, and summoned the governor of Si Province, Ma Xianbi. Xianbi wrote to Jing Province requesting troops to come to their aid.

sentences.zh: 衆咸謂宜待臺報，秀曰：「彼待我而爲援，援之宜速，待敕雖舊，非應急也。

translations.literal: All said one should wait for word from the capital; Xiu said: "They are waiting for Us as their support; support should be swift—waiting for an edict is the old way, but not what urgency requires.
translations.idiomatic: All said they should wait for orders from the capital. Xiu said, "They are waiting for us as their support. Aid should be swift. Waiting for an edict is the old way, but not what urgency requires.

sentences.zh: 」卽遣兵赴之。

translations.literal: " He immediately dispatched troops to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately dispatched troops to their aid.

sentences.zh: 先是，巴陵馬營蠻爲緣江寇害，後軍司馬高江產以郢州軍伐之，不剋，江產死之，蠻遂盛。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Maying barbarians of Baling had been river-bandits along the Yangzi; Rear Army Major Gao Jiangchan led Ying Province troops against them but could not overcome them; Jiangchan died in the campaign and the barbarians grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Maying barbarians of Baling had raided along the Yangzi. Rear Army Major Gao Jiangchan led troops from Ying Province against them but failed to subdue them; Jiangchan died in the campaign, and the barbarians grew stronger still.

sentences.zh: 秀遣防閤文熾率衆討之，燔其林木，絕其蹊逕，蠻失其嶮，期歲而江路清，於是州境盜賊遂絕。

translations.literal: Xiu sent his aide Wen Chi at the head of troops to attack them, burning their forests and cutting off their paths; the barbarians lost their strong positions, and within a year the river route was cleared—thereafter bandits in the province disappeared entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu sent his aide Wen Chi at the head of troops to attack them, burning their forests and cutting off their paths. Deprived of their strongholds, the barbarians were broken within a year and the river route was cleared; banditry in the province ceased altogether.

sentences.zh: 及沮水暴長，頗敗民田，秀以榖二萬斛贍之。

translations.literal: When the Ju River suddenly rose and greatly damaged the people's fields, Xiu used twenty thousand hu of grain to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ju River suddenly flooded and ruined much of the people's cropland, Xiu distributed twenty thousand hu of grain in relief.

sentences.zh: 使長史蕭琛簡府州貧老單丁吏，一日散遣五百餘人，百姓甚悅。

translations.literal: He had Chief Clerk Xiao Chen select from the prefectural and provincial staff poor elderly men and sole-support clerks, and in one day dismissed more than five hundred; the common people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He had Chief Clerk Xiao Chen identify poor elderly men and sole-support clerks among the prefectural and provincial staff, and in a single day dismissed more than five hundred of them. The people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 十一年，徵爲侍中、中衛將軍，領宗正卿、石頭戍事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned to serve as Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan and overseer of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was recalled to serve as palace attendant and central guard general, while concurrently directing the imperial clan office and overseeing the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督郢司霍三州諸軍事、安西將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he went out again as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Ying, Si, and Huo, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was posted again as bearer of the staff of authority, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, commander of military affairs in Ying, Si, and Huo, general who pacifies the west, and governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 郢州當塗爲劇地，百姓貧，至以婦人供役，其弊如此。

translations.literal: Ying Province at Dangtu was a harsh posting; the people were poor, to the point that women were pressed into corvée labor—such were its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Province at Dangtu was a harsh posting. The people were so poor that women were pressed into corvée labor; such were the abuses he inherited.

sentences.zh: 秀至鎮，務安之。

translations.literal: When Xiu reached his post, he devoted himself to bringing peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu took up his post, he devoted himself to bringing the region peace.

sentences.zh: 主者或求召吏。

translations.literal: The stewards sometimes requested that clerks be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: His staff sometimes requested that additional clerks be summoned.

sentences.zh: 秀曰：「不識救弊之術；

translations.literal: Xiu said: "You do not understand the art of remedying abuses;
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "You do not understand how to remedy abuses.

sentences.zh: 此州凋殘，不可擾也。

translations.literal: this province is wasted and broken—it must not be disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: This province is wasted and broken; it must not be disturbed further."

sentences.zh: 」於是務存約己，省去游費，百姓安堵，境內晏然。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he strove to restrain himself, cut traveling expenses, and the people lived in security; within the borders all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he strove to live simply, cut traveling expenses, and the people lived in security; within his jurisdiction all was tranquil.

sentences.zh: 先是夏口常爲兵沖，露骸積骨於黃鶴樓下，秀祭而埋之。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiakou had often been a battleground; exposed bones lay heaped below the Yellow Crane Tower, and Xiu performed rites and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiakou had long been a battleground, and exposed bones lay heaped below the Yellow Crane Tower. Xiu performed rites and buried them.

sentences.zh: 一夜，夢數百人拜謝而去。

translations.literal: One night he dreamed that several hundred people bowed in thanks and departed.
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed that several hundred people bowed to him in thanks and departed.

sentences.zh: 每冬月，常作襦褲以賜凍者。

translations.literal: Every winter month he would make padded jackets and trousers to give to those suffering from the cold.
translations.idiomatic: Every winter he had padded jackets and trousers made and distributed to those suffering from the cold.

sentences.zh: 時司州叛蠻田魯生，弟魯賢、超秀，據蒙籠來降。

translations.literal: At that time the rebellious barbarian Tian Lusheng of Si Province, with his younger brothers Lu Xian and Chao Xiu, held Menglong and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebellious barbarian Tian Lusheng of Si Province, together with his younger brothers Lu Xian and Chao Xiu, held Menglong and came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖以魯生爲北司州刺史，魯賢北豫州刺史，超秀定州刺史，爲北境捍蔽。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor made Lusheng Governor of Northern Si Province, Lu Xian Governor of Northern Yu, and Chao Xiu Governor of Ding Province, to serve as bulwarks of the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu appointed Lusheng governor of northern Si Province, Lu Xian governor of northern Yu, and Chao Xiu governor of Ding Province, to serve as bulwarks of the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 而魯生、超秀互相讒毀，有去就心，秀撫喻懷納，各得其用，當時賴之。

translations.literal: But Lusheng and Chao Xiu slandered each other and were inclined to come or go; Xiu soothed and embraced them, and each was put to good use—the age relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: But Lusheng and Chao Xiu slandered each other and were ready to defect. Xiu won them over with reassurance and put each to good use; the court relied on him for this.

sentences.zh: 初，秀之西也，郢州民相送出境，聞其疾，百姓商賈咸爲請命。

translations.literal: When Xiu first went west, the people of Ying Province escorted him beyond the border; when they heard of his illness, commoners and merchants alike all petitioned for his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu first went west, the people of Ying Province escorted him beyond the provincial border. When they heard of his illness, commoners and merchants alike petitioned for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 旣薨，四州民裂裳爲白帽，哀哭以迎送之。

translations.literal: After he died, the people of four provinces tore their garments to make white mourning caps and received and sent off his coffin with wailing lament.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, people in four provinces tore their garments to make white mourning caps and received and escorted his coffin with wailing lament.

sentences.zh: 雍州蠻迎秀，聞薨，祭哭而去。

translations.literal: Barbarians of Yong Province had come to welcome Xiu; when they heard of his death, they performed rites, wept, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians of Yong Province had come out to welcome Xiu; when they heard of his death, they performed rites, wept, and departed.

sentences.zh: 喪至京師，高祖使使册贈侍中、司空，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, the High Ancestor sent envoys to confer posthumously Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached the capital, Emperor Wu sent envoys to confer posthumously the titles of palace attendant and minister of works. His posthumous title was Kang, "Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 秀有容觀，每朝，百僚屬目。

translations.literal: Xiu had fine appearance and bearing; at every court session the hundred officials fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had a fine appearance and bearing; at every court session the officials fixed their eyes on him.

sentences.zh: 性仁恕，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: His nature was benevolent and forgiving; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He was benevolent and forgiving by nature; joy and anger never showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 左右嘗以石擲殺所養鵠，齋帥請治其罪。

translations.literal: Once a attendant killed a goose he kept by throwing a stone at it; the steward of his fast asked that the offender be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Once an attendant killed a goose Xiu kept by throwing a stone at it. The steward of his household asked that the offender be punished.

sentences.zh: 秀曰：「吾豈以鳥傷人。

translations.literal: Xiu said: "How could I harm a person on account of a bird."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "How could I harm a person on account of a bird."

sentences.zh: 」在京師，旦臨公事，廚人進食，誤而覆之，去而登車，竟朝不飯，亦不之誚也。

translations.literal: " In the capital, one morning as he was attending to public business the cook brought food and accidentally overturned it; Xiu left and boarded his carriage, went the whole court session without eating, and did not reprove the man.
translations.idiomatic: " In the capital, one morning as he attended to public business the cook brought food and accidentally overturned it. Xiu left and boarded his carriage, went through the entire court session without eating, and never reproved the man.

sentences.zh: 精意術學，搜集經記，招學士平原劉孝標，使撰《類苑》，書未及畢，而已行於世。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to the arts and learning, gathered classics and records, and recruited the scholar Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan to compile the Garden of Categories; the book was not yet finished but portions were already circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to scholarship, gathered classics and records, and recruited the scholar Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan to compile the Garden of Categories. The book was not yet finished, but portions were already circulating.

sentences.zh: 秀于高祖布衣昆弟，及爲君臣，小心畏敬，過於疏賤者，高祖益以此賢之。

translations.literal: Xiu and the High Ancestor had been brothers in common cloth; when they became sovereign and subject, his careful reverence exceeded that of distant and lowly men, and the High Ancestor esteemed him all the more for this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and Emperor Wu had been brothers in humble circumstances. Once they became sovereign and subject, Xiu's careful reverence exceeded that shown by distant and lowly men, and the emperor esteemed him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 少偏孤，於始興王嶦尤篤。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was especially devoted to the Prince of Shixing Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was especially devoted to Prince Shixing, Dan.

sentences.zh: 梁興，嶦久爲荊州刺史，自天監初，常以所得俸中分與秀，秀稱心受之，亦弗辭多也。

translations.literal: When Liang arose, Dan long served as Governor of Jing Province; from the beginning of Tianjian he regularly shared half his salary with Xiu, and Xiu gladly accepted it, never declining even when the share was large.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang dynasty was founded, Dan long served as governor of Jing Province. From the beginning of Tianjian he regularly shared half his salary with Xiu, who gladly accepted and never declined even when the share was large.

sentences.zh: 昆弟之睦，時議歸之。

translations.literal: The harmony between the brothers was what public opinion commended in them.
translations.idiomatic: The harmony between the brothers was what contemporaries most admired in them.

sentences.zh: 故吏夏侯稟等表立墓碑，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Former subordinates Xiahou Bing and others memorialized to erect a tomb stele; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Former subordinates Xiahou Bing and others memorialized to erect a tomb stele, and an edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 當世高才游王門者，東海王僧孺、吳郡陸倕、彭城劉孝綽、河東裴子野，各制其文，古未之有也。

translations.literal: Men of eminent talent of the age who frequented princely gates—Wang Sengru of Donghai, Lu Yan of Wu Commandery, Liu Xiaochuo of Pengcheng, and Pei Ziye of Hedong—each composed a text for the stele; nothing like it had existed in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The leading literary figures of the age who frequented princely courts—Wang Sengru of Donghai, Lu Yan of Wu, Liu Xiaochuo of Pengcheng, and Pei Ziye of Hedong—each composed a text for the stele. Nothing like it had existed in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 世子機嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Ji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent, Ji, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 機字智通，天監二年，除安成國世子。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Zhitong, in the second year of Tianjian was appointed heir of the State of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose style was Zhitong, was appointed heir of the state of Ancheng in the second year of Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 六年，爲寧遠將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became General of Pacification at a Distance and Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed general of pacification at a distance and governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 還爲給事中。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as attendant within the gates.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，襲封安成郡王，其年爲太子洗馬，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Ancheng Commandery; that year he became Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud and was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong he inherited the title Prince of Ancheng, and that same year became groom of the crown prince's stud before being promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷明威將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to General of Manifest Might and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed general of manifest might and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷持節、督湘衡桂三州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Xiang, Heng, and Gui, General of Pacification at a Distance, and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Xiang, Heng, and Gui, general of pacification at a distance, and governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 大通二年，薨于州，時年三十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he died in the province, at the age of thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he died in office, at the age of thirty.

sentences.zh: 機美姿容，善吐納。

translations.literal: Ji had handsome looks and was skilled in breath regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was handsome and skilled in breath-regulation exercises.

sentences.zh: 家旣多書，博學強記；

translations.literal: His household had many books, and he was broadly learned with a powerful memory;
translations.idiomatic: His household possessed many books, and he was broadly learned with a powerful memory;

sentences.zh: 然而好弄，尚力，遠士子，近小人。

translations.literal: yet he loved horseplay, valued brute strength, kept distant from gentlemen, and drew near to petty men.
translations.idiomatic: yet he loved horseplay, valued brute strength, kept his distance from gentlemen, and drew near to petty men.

sentences.zh: 爲州專意聚斂，無治績，頻被案劾。

translations.literal: As governor he devoted himself solely to amassing wealth, had no record of good governance, and was repeatedly investigated and impeached.
translations.idiomatic: As governor he devoted himself solely to amassing wealth, achieved nothing in governance, and was repeatedly investigated and impeached.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，有司請諡，高祖詔曰：「王好內怠政，可諡曰煬。

translations.literal: When he was about to be buried, the relevant offices requested a posthumous title; the High Ancestor decreed: "The prince was fond of the inner quarters and negligent in government—his posthumous title may be Yang."
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to be buried, the relevant offices requested a posthumous title. Emperor Wu decreed, "The prince was fond of his harem and negligent in government. His posthumous title shall be Yang, 'Dissolute.'"

sentences.zh: 」所著詩賦數千言，世祖集而序之。

translations.literal: " The poems and rhapsodies he composed, several thousand words in all, were collected and prefaced by the Shizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " The poems and rhapsodies he composed, several thousand words in all, were collected and prefaced by Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子操嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 南浦侯推，字智進，機次弟也。

translations.literal: Marquis Tui of Nanpu, styled Zhijin, was Ji's next younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Tui of Nanpu, whose style was Zhijin, was Ji's next younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少清敏，好屬文，深爲太宗所賞。

translations.literal: In youth he was clear-minded and quick, loved literary composition, and was deeply appreciated by the Taizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was quick-witted and clear-minded, loved literary composition, and was deeply favored by Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 普通六年，以王子例封。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong he was enfeoffed by the precedent for princes' sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Putong he was enfeoffed according to the precedent for princes' sons.

sentences.zh: 歷寧遠將軍、淮南太守。

translations.literal: He served successively as General of Pacification at a Distance and Governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as general of pacification at a distance and governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 遷輕車將軍、晉陵太守，給事中，太子洗馬，秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Light Chariots and Governor of Jinling, Attendant Within the Gates, Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud, and Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the light chariots and governor of Jinling, and also served as attendant within the gates, groom of the crown prince's stud, and secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出爲戎昭將軍、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Martial Brilliance and Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as general of martial brilliance and governor of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 所臨必赤地大旱，吳人號「旱母」焉。

translations.literal: Wherever he was posted the land turned red with great drought, and the people of Wu called him "the Drought Mother."
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he was posted the land suffered severe drought, and the people of Wu called him "the Drought Mother."

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，守東府城，賊設樓車，盡銳攻之，推隨方抗拒，頻擊挫之。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he defended the Eastern Palace city; the rebels set up siege towers and attacked with all their elite forces, but Tui resisted on every side and repeatedly struck them down.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he defended the Eastern Palace city. The rebels set up siege towers and attacked with all their elite forces, but Tui resisted on every side and repeatedly repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 至夕，東北樓主許鬱華啓關延賊，城遂陷，推握節死之。

translations.literal: By evening the commander of the northeast tower, Xu Yuhua, opened the gate and admitted the rebels; the city fell, and Tui grasped his staff and died.
translations.idiomatic: By evening the commander of the northeast tower, Xu Yuhua, opened the gate and admitted the rebels. The city fell, and Tui grasped his command baton and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 南平元襄王偉字文達，太祖第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping Wei, styled Wenda, was the eighth son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping, Wei, whose style was Wenda, was the founding emperor's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 幼清警好學。

translations.literal: In youth he was clear-minded, alert, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was alert, clear-minded, and fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 齊世，起家晉安鎮北法曹行參軍府，遷驃騎，轉外兵。

translations.literal: Under Qi he began his career as Acting Army Aide of the Legal Bureau in the headquarters of the Pacifying North Army of Jin'an, was transferred to the Flying Cavalry command, and then moved to the outer bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he began his career as acting aide in the legal bureau of the Pacifying North Army at Jin'an, was transferred to the flying cavalry command, and then moved to the outer bureau.

sentences.zh: 高祖爲雍州，慮天下將亂，求迎偉及始興王忄詹來襄陽。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor was in Yong Province, fearing the realm would soon fall into disorder, he asked that Wei and the Prince of Shixing Dan be brought to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu was in Yong Province, fearing the realm would soon fall into disorder, he asked that Wei and Prince Shixing be brought to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 俄聞已入沔，高祖欣然謂佐吏曰：「吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: Soon he heard they had entered the Mian region; the High Ancestor said with delight to his staff: "I have no more worries.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he heard they had entered the Han River region. He said with delight to his staff, "I have no more worries.

sentences.zh: 」義師起，南康王承制，板爲冠軍將軍，留行雍州開府事。

translations.literal: " When the righteous army rose, the Prince of Nankang assumed the regency and appointed him General of the Champion Army, leaving him to handle the affairs of the open office of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: " When the righteous army rose, Prince Nankang assumed the regency and appointed him general of the champion army, leaving him to manage the affairs of the Yong Province headquarters.

sentences.zh: 義師發後，州內儲備及人皆虛竭。

translations.literal: After the righteous army set out, stores within the province and its manpower were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the righteous army set out, the province's stores and manpower were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 魏興太守裴師仁、齊興太守顏僧都並據郡不受命，舉兵將襲雍州，偉與始興王嶦遣兵于始平郡待師仁等，要擊大破之，州境以安。

translations.literal: The Governors of Weixing Pei Shiren and Qixing Yan Sengdu each held their commanderies and refused orders, raising troops to strike Yong Province; Wei and the Prince of Shixing Dan sent troops to wait for Shiren and the others in Shiping Commandery, intercepted them, and inflicted a great defeat—the province was thereby secured.
translations.idiomatic: The governors of Weixing, Pei Shiren, and Qixing, Yan Sengdu, each held their commanderies and refused orders, raising troops to strike Yong Province. Wei and Prince Shixing sent troops to wait for them in Shiping Commandery, intercepted them, and inflicted a great defeat, securing the province.

sentences.zh: 高祖旣剋郢、魯，下尋陽，圍建業，而巴東太守蕭慧訓子璝及巴西太守魯休烈起兵逼荊州，屯軍上明，連破荊州。

translations.literal: After the High Ancestor had taken Ying and Lu, advanced down to Xunyang, and besieged Jiankang, the Governor of Badong Xiao Huixun's son Gui and the Governor of Baxi Lu Xiulie raised troops to press Jing Province, encamped at Shangming, and repeatedly defeated Jing forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu had taken Ying and Lu, advanced to Xunyang, and besieged Jiankang, the son of the governor of Badong, Xiao Huixun, Gui, and the governor of Baxi, Lu Xiulie, raised troops against Jing Province, encamped at Shangming, and repeatedly defeated Jing forces.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍蕭穎胄遣將劉孝慶等距之，反爲璝所敗，穎胄憂憤暴疾卒，西朝兇懼。

translations.literal: The Stabilizing Army Xiao Yingzhou sent the generals Liu Xiaoqing and others to resist them but was in turn defeated by Gui; Yingzhou died suddenly of grief and rage, and the western court was seized with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingzhou, stabilizing general of Jing Province, sent Liu Xiaoqing and others to resist them but was defeated by Gui. Yingzhou died suddenly of grief and rage, and the western court was seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射夏侯詳議徵兵雍州，偉乃割州府將吏，配始興王嶦往赴之。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xiahou Xiang proposed recruiting troops from Yong Province; Wei then allotted the province's generals and officials to the Prince of Shixing Dan to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xiahou Xiang proposed recruiting troops from Yong Province. Wei then assigned the province's generals and officials to Prince Shixing to go to their aid.

sentences.zh: 嶦旣至，璝等皆降。

translations.literal: When Dan arrived, Gui and the others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan arrived, Gui and the others all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 和帝詔以偉爲使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Emperor He decreed that Wei should be Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, Jingling in Ying Province, and Suizhou in Si Province, Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong Province, with his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He decreed that Wei should be bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, southern Qin, and northern Qin, as well as Jingling in Ying Province and Suizhou in Si Province, colonel pacifying the barbarians, and governor of Yong Province, with his general's title unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中，進號鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Palace Attendant and advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed palace attendant and promoted to general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，加散騎常侍，進督荊、寧二州，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and advanced to command Jing and Ning as well, with the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he was additionally appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and given command over Jing and Ning as well, with his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 封建安郡王，食邑二千戶，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an Commandery with a fief of two thousand households and granted a set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Prince of Jian'an with a fief of two thousand households and granted a set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙都督南徐州諸軍事、南徐州刺史，使持節、常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Southern Xu and Governor of Southern Xu, with Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant, and General unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to commander of military affairs in southern Xu and governor of southern Xu, while retaining his titles as bearer of the staff of authority, regular attendant, and general.

sentences.zh: 五年，至都，改爲撫軍將軍、丹陽尹，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he reached the capital and was changed to General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang, with Regular Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he reached the capital and was appointed general who pacifies the army and intendant of Danyang, while retaining his post as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷使持節、都督揚、南徐二州諸軍事、右軍將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yang and Southern Xu, General of the Right Army, and Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Yang and southern Xu, general of the right army, and governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 未拜，進號中權將軍。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment, his title was advanced to General of the Central Authority.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the appointment, his title was advanced to general of the central authority.

sentences.zh: 七年，以疾表解州，改侍中、中撫軍，知司徒事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on account of illness he memorialized to resign the governorship and was changed to Palace Attendant, Central Pacifying General, with charge of the Minister of Education's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, on account of illness he memorialized to resign the governorship and was appointed palace attendant and central pacifying general, with charge of the minister of education's affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷護軍、石頭戍軍事，侍中、將軍、鼓吹如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Protector of the Army and overseer of the Shitou garrison, with Palace Attendant, General, and martial music unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed protector of the army and overseer of the Shitou garrison, while retaining his posts as palace attendant and general and his grant of martial music.

sentences.zh: 其年，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督江州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、江州刺史，鼓吹如故。

translations.literal: That year he went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Jiang Province, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Jiang Province, with martial music unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was posted as bearer of the staff of authority, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, commander of military affairs in Jiang Province, general who pacifies the south, and governor of Jiang Province, with his grant of martial music unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以本號加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, with his existing title he was given the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies with an open office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was granted the ceremonial privileges of the three excellencies with an open office in addition to his existing title.

sentences.zh: 其年，復以疾陳解。

translations.literal: That year he again memorialized to resign on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: That year he again memorialized to resign on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 十二年，徵爲撫軍將軍，儀同、常侍如故，以疾不拜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the Army, with ceremonial privileges and Regular Attendant unchanged, but on account of illness he did not take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was summoned as general who pacifies the army, with his ceremonial privileges and post as regular attendant unchanged, but on account of illness he did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改爲左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed grand master of splendid happiness on the left.

sentences.zh: 加親信四十人，歲給米萬斛，布絹五千匹，藥直二百四十萬，廚供月二十萬，并二衛兩營雜役二百人，倍先。

translations.literal: He was given forty trusted attendants; annually ten thousand hu of rice, five thousand bolts of cloth and silk, two million four hundred thousand in medicine allowance, two hundred thousand monthly for kitchen supplies, and two hundred miscellaneous laborers from the two guards and two camps—double the former allotment.
translations.idiomatic: He was given forty trusted attendants; annually ten thousand hu of rice, five thousand bolts of cloth and silk, 2.4 million in medicine allowance, and 200,000 monthly for kitchen supplies, together with two hundred miscellaneous laborers from the two guards and two camps—double his former allotment.

sentences.zh: 置防閤白直左右職局一百人。

translations.literal: A staff of one hundred aides, white-uniformed attendants, and left and right office personnel was established for him.
translations.idiomatic: A staff of one hundred aides, attendants, and office personnel was established for him.

sentences.zh: 偉末年疾浸劇，不復出籓，故俸秩加焉。

translations.literal: In his later years Wei's illness grew steadily worse and he no longer went out to a provincial post, and for this reason his salary and rank were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Wei's illness grew steadily worse and he no longer took up provincial office; for this reason his salary and perquisites were increased.

sentences.zh: 偉少好學，篤誠通恕，趨賢重士，常如不及。

translations.literal: Wei from youth loved learning; he was sincere, open, and forgiving, and in hastening to honor the worthy and esteem gentlemen he always seemed not to be keeping pace.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wei loved learning. He was sincere, open, and forgiving, and in honoring the worthy and esteeming gentlemen he always seemed unable to do enough.

sentences.zh: 由是四方遊士，當世知名者，莫不畢至。

translations.literal: For this reason wandering scholars from the four directions and men renowned in the age—none failed to come.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason wandering scholars from every direction and every renowned man of the age came to him without exception.

sentences.zh: 齊世，青溪宮改爲芳林苑，天監初，賜偉爲第，偉又加穿築，增植嘉樹珍果，窮極雕麗，每與賓客遊其中，命從事中郎蕭子範爲之記。

translations.literal: Under Qi the Qingxi Palace was changed to the Fanglin Park; at the beginning of Tianjian it was granted to Wei as his residence, and Wei further excavated and built, adding fine trees and rare fruits until the ornamentation reached the utmost splendor; he would roam there with guests and had his aide Xiao Zifan compose a record of it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi the Qingxi Palace had been converted into the Fanglin Park. At the beginning of Tianjian it was granted to Wei as his residence, and he further excavated and built, planting fine trees and rare fruits until the ornamentation reached the utmost splendor. He would roam there with guests and had his aide Xiao Zifan compose a record of the estate.

sentences.zh: 梁世籓邸之盛，無以過焉。

translations.literal: Among the splendor of princely residences in the Liang age, none surpassed it.
translations.idiomatic: Among the splendor of princely residences in the Liang age, none surpassed it.

sentences.zh: 而性多恩惠，尤愍窮乏。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was full of kindness, and he was especially moved by the poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was full of kindness, and he was especially moved by the poor and destitute.

sentences.zh: 常遣腹心左右，歷訪閭里人士，其有貧困吉凶不舉者，卽遣贍卹之。

translations.literal: He regularly sent trusted attendants to visit people in the lanes and hamlets; whenever he found those in poverty or unable to manage auspicious and inauspicious occasions, he immediately sent relief and support.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly sent trusted attendants to visit people in the lanes and hamlets. Whenever they found those in poverty or unable to manage weddings and funerals, he immediately sent relief.

sentences.zh: 太原王曼穎卒，家貧無以殯斂，友人江革往哭之，其妻兒對革號訴。

translations.literal: Wang Manying of Taiyuan died; his family was too poor to bury him, and his friend Jiang Ge went to mourn; his wife and children faced Ge with wailing appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Manying of Taiyuan died, and his family was too poor to bury him. His friend Jiang Ge went to mourn, and Wang's wife and children faced him with wailing appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 革曰：「建安王當知，必爲營理。

translations.literal: Ge said: "The Prince of Jian'an will surely know and will certainly arrange matters."
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "Prince Jian'an will surely hear of this and will certainly arrange the funeral."

sentences.zh: 」言未訖而偉使至，給其喪事，得周濟焉。

translations.literal: " Before he had finished speaking Wei's envoy arrived and provided for the funeral; they received full relief.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he had finished speaking, Wei's envoy arrived and provided for the funeral. The family received full relief.

sentences.zh: 每祁寒積雪，則遣人載樵米，隨乏絕者卽賦給之。

translations.literal: Whenever severe cold brought heavy snow, he sent men with carts of firewood and rice to give to those in want as soon as their supplies ran out.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever severe cold brought heavy snow, he sent men with carts of firewood and rice to distribute to those whose supplies had run out.

sentences.zh: 晚年崇信佛理，尤精玄學，著《二旨義》，別爲新通。

translations.literal: In his later years he revered Buddhist principles and was especially accomplished in Dark Learning; he authored The Meaning of the Two Aims, setting forth a new understanding.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he revered Buddhist teachings and was especially accomplished in Dark Learning. He authored The Meaning of the Two Aims, setting forth a new understanding.

sentences.zh: 又制《性情》、《幾神》等論其義，僧寵及周捨、殷鈞、陸倕並名精解，而不能屈。

translations.literal: He also composed On Nature and Sentiment, On the Subtle Spirit, and other treatises expounding its meaning; Seng Chong, Zhou She, Yin Jun, and Lu Yan were all famed for penetrating understanding, yet none could refute him.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed On Nature and Sentiment, On the Subtle Spirit, and other treatises expounding its meaning. Seng Chong, Zhou She, Yin Jun, and Lu Yan were all famed for penetrating understanding, yet none could refute him.

sentences.zh: 偉四子：恪，恭，虔，祗。

translations.literal: Wei had four sons: Ke, Geng, Qian, and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had four sons: Ke, Geng, Qian, and Zhi.

sentences.zh: 世子恪嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Ke succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Ke succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 恭字敬範。

translations.literal: Geng's style was Jingfan.
translations.idiomatic: Geng, styled Jingfan.

sentences.zh: 天監八年，封衡山縣侯，以元襄功，加邑至千戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hengshan; on account of Yuanxiang's merit his fief was increased to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hengshan; on account of Prince Yuanxiang's merit his fief was increased to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 初，樂山侯正則有罪，勑讓諸王，獨謂元襄曰：「汝兒非直無過，並有義方。」

translations.literal: At the beginning the Marquis of Leshan Zhengze committed an offense; an imperial command rebuked the princes, but to Yuanxiang alone it said: "Your sons are not only without fault—they also possess proper conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Marquis of Leshan, Zhengze, had committed an offense, an imperial edict rebuked the princes but said to Prince Yuanxiang alone: "Your sons are not only without fault—they also possess proper conduct."

sentences.zh: 恭起家給事中，遷太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Geng began his career as Palace Attendant and was promoted to Groom of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Geng began his career as palace attendant and was promoted to groom of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 出爲督齊安等十一郡事、寧遠將軍、西陽武昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as supervisor of the affairs of eleven commanderies including Qi'an, as General Who Pacifies the Distance, and as governor of the two commanderies of Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as supervisor of eleven commanderies including Qi'an, as general who pacifies the distance, and as governor of Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 徵爲秘書丞，遷中書郎，監丹陽尹，行徐南徐州事，轉衡州刺史，母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Secretary Director, promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, supervised the Commandant of Danyang, acted in the affairs of Xu and Southern Xuzhou, transferred to Governor of Hengzhou, and left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as secretary director, promoted to secretariat gentleman, supervised the commandant of Danyang, acted in the affairs of Xu and southern Xuzhou, transferred to governor of Hengzhou, and left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 尋起爲雲麾將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Cloud-Banner General and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as cloud-banner general and governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭善解吏事，所在見稱。

translations.literal: Geng was skilled at understanding administrative affairs and was praised wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Geng was skilled at administrative affairs and won praise wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 而性尚華侈，廣營第宅，重齋步櫩，模寫宮殿。

translations.literal: Yet his nature inclined toward splendor and extravagance; he extensively built mansions, with heavy halls and covered walkways, modeled after palace architecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature inclined toward splendor and extravagance. He extensively built mansions with heavy halls and covered walkways modeled after palace architecture.

sentences.zh: 尤好賓友，酣讌終辰，座客滿筵，言談不倦。

translations.literal: He especially loved guests and friends, feasting until the day's end with the seats filled and conversation never flagging.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved entertaining guests and friends, feasting until day's end with every seat filled and conversation never flagging.

sentences.zh: 時世祖居籓，頗事聲譽，勤心著述，卮酒未嘗妄進。

translations.literal: At that time the Shizu Emperor was in his princely fief, quite cultivating his reputation, diligently applying himself to writing, and never casually offering a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yuan was in his princely fief, quite cultivating his reputation, diligently devoting himself to writing, and never casually offering a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 恭每從容謂人曰：「下官歷觀世人，多有不好歡樂，乃仰眠床上，看屋梁而著書，千秋萬歲，誰傳此者。

translations.literal: Geng would calmly say to people: "I have observed many people in the world who do not enjoy pleasure but lie on their backs in bed, look at the roof beams, and compose books—after a thousand or ten thousand years, who will transmit such things?
translations.idiomatic: Geng would calmly remark to others: "I have observed many people in the world who eschew pleasure, lying on their backs in bed gazing at the roof beams and composing books—after a thousand or ten thousand years, who will pass such things down?

sentences.zh: 勞神苦思，竟不成名，豈如臨清風，對朗月，登山泛水，肆意酣歌也。

translations.literal: They labor their spirits and think bitterly, yet in the end achieve no fame—how can that compare with facing the clear breeze, meeting the bright moon, climbing mountains, boating on the waters, and singing freely in intoxication?
translations.idiomatic: They tax their minds and think bitterly, yet in the end achieve no fame—how can that compare with facing a clear breeze beneath a bright moon, climbing mountains and boating on the waters, and singing freely in drunken abandon?

sentences.zh: 」尋以雍州蠻文道拘引魏寇，詔恭赴援，仍除持節、仁威將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，便道之鎮。

translations.literal: " Soon, because the barbarians of Yongzhou led by Wen Dao induced Wei invaders, an edict summoned Geng to go to their aid; he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Renwei, Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Governor of Yongzhou, and proceeded by the direct route to his post.
