translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward, because the Yongzhou barbarian Wen Dao had induced Northern Wei invaders, an edict summoned Geng to aid the province. He was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, General Renwei, colonel who pacifies the barbarians, and governor of Yongzhou, and proceeded by the direct route to his post.

sentences.zh: 太宗少與恭遊，特被賞狎，至是手令曰：「彼士流骯髒，有關輔餘風，黔首扞格，但知重劍輕死。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor from youth had associated with Geng and was especially favored and intimate with him; on this occasion he sent a personal order saying: "The gentry there are coarse and filthy, retaining the residual customs of Guanfu; the common people are stubborn and defiant, knowing only to value swords and lightly regard death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen had associated with Geng from youth and was especially fond of him. On this occasion he sent a personal order saying: "The gentry there are coarse and filthy, retaining the residual customs of the Guanzhong region; the common people are stubborn and defiant, knowing only to value swords and lightly regard death.

sentences.zh: 降胡惟尚貪惏，邊蠻不知敬讓，懷抱不可皁白，法律無所用施。

translations.literal: The surrendered Hu care only for greed; the border barbarians know nothing of respect and yielding; their inner thoughts cannot be clarified as black or white, and laws have no application.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered Hu care only for greed; the border barbarians know nothing of respect and yielding; their inner thoughts cannot be easily read, and laws have no purchase there.

sentences.zh: 願充實邊戍，無數遷徙，諜候惟遠，箱庾惟積，長以控短，靜以制躁。

translations.literal: I wish you to fill and strengthen the border garrisons, avoid frequent relocations, keep spies only at a distance, store grain in granaries, use length to control shortness, and use stillness to restrain restlessness.
translations.idiomatic: I wish you to strengthen the border garrisons, avoid frequent relocations, keep scouts far afield, accumulate grain in storehouses, use length to control shortness, and use stillness to restrain restlessness.

sentences.zh: 早蒙愛念，敢布腹心。

translations.literal: Having long received your affectionate regard, I venture to lay open my innermost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Having long enjoyed your affection, I venture to lay open my innermost thoughts.

sentences.zh: 」恭至州，治果有聲績，百姓陳奏，乞於城南立碑頌德，詔許焉。

translations.literal: " When Geng arrived at the province his governance indeed won renown and achievement; the common people submitted petitions asking that a stele be erected south of the city to praise his virtue, and the edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: " When Geng arrived in the province his governance indeed won reputation and achievement. The people submitted petitions asking that a stele be erected south of the city in praise of his virtue, and the edict granted their request.

sentences.zh: 先高祖以雍爲邊鎮，運數州之粟，以實儲倉，恭後多取官米，贍給私宅，爲荊州刺史廬陵王所啓，由是免官削爵，數年竟不敘用。

translations.literal: Formerly the High Ancestor had made Yong a border post and transported grain from several prefectures to fill the storehouses; Geng later took much official grain to supply his private residence, and this was reported by the Prince of Luling as Governor of Jingzhou; for this reason he was dismissed from office and stripped of his rank, and for several years was ultimately not reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wu had made Yong a border post and transported grain from several prefectures to fill the storehouses. Geng later took much official grain to supply his private residence. The Prince of Luling, as governor of Jingzhou, reported this, and for this reason Geng was dismissed and stripped of his rank; for several years he received no reappointment.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，卒于城中，時年五十二。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he died in the city, at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he died in the city, at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔特復本封。

translations.literal: An edict specially restored his original enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially restored his original enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 世祖追贈侍中、左衛將軍。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor posthumously granted him Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan posthumously granted him attendant-in-ordinary and left guard general.

sentences.zh: 諡曰僖。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Xi.

sentences.zh: 世子靜，字安仁，有美名，號爲宗室後進。

translations.literal: The heir Jing, styled Anren, had a fine reputation and was hailed as the outstanding successor among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Jing, styled Anren, enjoyed a fine reputation and was hailed as the outstanding young member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 有文才，而篤志好學，旣內足於財，多聚經史，散書滿席，手自讎校。

translations.literal: He had literary talent and a steadfast love of learning; since he was amply provided with wealth within, he gathered many classics and histories, books scattered to fill his mat, and collated them with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He had literary talent and devoted himself steadfastly to learning. Since he was amply provided with wealth, he gathered many classics and histories until books scattered across his mat, and collated them with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 何敬容欲以女妻之，靜忌其太盛，距而不納，時論服焉。

translations.literal: He Jingrong wished to give his daughter to him in marriage, but Jing feared that family was too powerful and refused without accepting; contemporary opinion admired him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He Jingrong wished to give his daughter to him in marriage, but Jing feared that family was too powerful and declined; contemporary opinion admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 歷官太子舍人、東宮領直。

translations.literal: He held the offices of Attendant of the Crown Prince and Director of Attendance in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant of the crown prince and director of attendance in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷丹陽尹丞，給事黃門侍郎，深爲太宗所愛賞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to aide to the Commandant of Danyang and Supervising Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, and was deeply loved and appreciated by the Taizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to aide to the commandant of Danyang and supervising gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, and was deeply loved and favored by Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing he died and was posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing he died and was posthumously granted attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽忠烈王恢字弘達，太祖第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhonglie of Poyang Hui, styled Hongda, was the ninth son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhonglie of Poyang, Hui, styled Hongda, was the founding emperor's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 幼聰穎，年七歲，能通《孝經》、《論語》義，發擿無所遺。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and quick; at the age of seven he could fully comprehend the meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, raising and probing questions without omitting anything.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and quick. At the age of seven he could fully comprehend the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, raising and probing questions without omitting anything.

sentences.zh: 旣長，美風表，涉獵史籍。

translations.literal: When he had grown up he had fine bearing and appearance and ranged broadly through historical records.
translations.idiomatic: When he had grown up he had a fine bearing and appearance and ranged broadly through historical records.

sentences.zh: 齊隆昌中，明帝作相，內外多虞，明帝就長沙宣武王懿求諸弟有可委以腹心者，宣武言恢焉。

translations.literal: In the Longchang era of Qi, when Emperor Ming was acting as grand counselor and anxieties were many at court and abroad, Emperor Ming asked Prince Xuanwu of Changsha Yi whether among his younger brothers there was one who could be entrusted with his innermost confidence; Prince Xuanwu named Hui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longchang era of Qi, when Emperor Ming was serving as grand counselor and anxieties were many at court and abroad, Emperor Ming asked Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, whether among his younger brothers there was one who could be entrusted with his innermost confidence, and Prince Xuanwu named Hui.

sentences.zh: 明帝以恢爲寧遠將軍，甲仗百人衛東府，且引爲驃騎法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming appointed Hui General Who Pacifies the Distance; a hundred armored guards protected the Eastern Palace, and he was additionally brought in as acting aide in the legal bureau under the Flying Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming appointed Hui general who pacifies the distance, with a hundred armored guards to protect the Eastern Palace, and additionally brought him in as acting aide in the legal bureau under the flying cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，東宮建，爲太子舍人，累遷北中郎外兵參軍，前軍主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne the Eastern Palace was established; Hui became Attendant of the Crown Prince and was progressively promoted to military aide under the Northern Central Commander and recorder in the merit bureau under the Vanguard General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne and the Eastern Palace was established, he became attendant of the crown prince and was progressively promoted to military aide under the northern central commander and recorder in the merit bureau under the vanguard general.

sentences.zh: 宣武之難，逃在京師。

translations.literal: During Prince Xuanwu's crisis he fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Prince Xuanwu's crisis he fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖義兵至，恢於新林奉迎，以爲輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor's volunteer army arrived, Hui went to Xinlin to welcome him and was appointed General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu's volunteer army arrived, Hui went to Xinlin to welcome him and was appointed general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 時三吳多亂，高祖命出頓破崗。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Wu regions were largely in disorder; the High Ancestor ordered him out to encamp at Pogang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Three Wu regions were largely in disorder, and Emperor Wu ordered him out to encamp at Pogang.

sentences.zh: 建康平，還爲冠軍將軍、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he returned and was made Champion General and Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified he returned and was appointed champion general and right guard general.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，爲侍中、前將軍，領石頭戍軍事，封鄱陽郡王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he became Attendant-in-Ordinary and Vanguard General, took charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Poyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he became attendant-in-ordinary and vanguard general, took charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Poyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二年，出爲使持節、都督南徐州諸軍事、征虜將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Southern Xuzhou, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and Governor of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in southern Xuzhou, general who conquers the barbarians, and governor of southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，改授都督郢司二州諸軍事、後將軍、郢州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his appointment was changed to Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the two provinces of Ying and Si, Rear General, and Governor of Yingzhou, with bearer of the staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his appointment was changed to commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ying and Si provinces, rear general, and governor of Yingzhou, with bearer of the staff unchanged.

sentences.zh: 義兵初，郢城內疾疫死者甚多，不及藏殯，及恢下車，遽命埋掩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the volunteer army campaign many in the city of Ying died of plague before their bodies could be properly interred; when Hui took up his post he immediately ordered them buried.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the volunteer army campaign many in the city of Ying had died of plague before their bodies could be properly interred. When Hui took up his post he immediately ordered them buried.

sentences.zh: 又遣四使巡行州部，境內大治。

translations.literal: He also dispatched four envoys to tour the commandery and the territory was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched four envoys to tour the commandery, and the territory was brought to excellent order.

sentences.zh: 七年，進號雲麾將軍，進督霍州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his title was advanced to Cloud-Banner General and he was given additional supervision over Huozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his title was advanced to cloud-banner general and he was given additional supervision over Huozhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，復進號平西將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his title was again advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his title was again advanced to general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 十年，徵爲侍中、護軍將軍、石頭戍軍事，領宗正卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Guards the Army, in charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison, and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, general who guards the army, in charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison, and concurrently director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出爲使持節、都督荊湘雍益寧南北梁南北秦九州諸軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the nine provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Ning, Southern Liang, Northern Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Jingzhou, and was given one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the nine provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Ning, southern Liang, northern Liang, southern Qin, and northern Qin, general who pacifies the west, and governor of Jingzhou, and was given one set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷散騎常侍、都督益寧南北秦沙七州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、益州刺史，使持節如故，便道之鎮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant at the Palace Gate, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the seven provinces of Yi, Ning, Southern Qin, Northern Qin, and Sha, General Who Guards the West, and Governor of Yizhou, with bearer of the staff unchanged, proceeding by the direct route to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to regular attendant at the palace gate, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the seven provinces of Yi, Ning, southern Qin, northern Qin, and Sha, general who guards the west, and governor of Yizhou, with bearer of the staff unchanged, and proceeded by the direct route to his post.

sentences.zh: 成都去新城五百里，陸路往來，悉訂私馬，百姓患焉，累政不能改。

translations.literal: From Chengdu to Xincheng was five hundred li; over land traffic all requisitioned private horses, to the people's distress, and successive administrations could not change this.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu was five hundred li from Xincheng. All land traffic requisitioned private horses, to the people's distress, and successive administrations could not change the practice.

sentences.zh: 恢乃市馬千匹，以付所訂之家，資其騎乘，有用則以次發之，百姓賴焉。

translations.literal: Hui then purchased a thousand horses and gave them to the families from whom horses were requisitioned, supplying them with mounts and issuing them in turn as needed; the people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then purchased a thousand horses and gave them to the families from whom horses were requisitioned, supplying them with mounts and issuing them in turn as needed, and the people benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 十七年，徵爲侍中、安前將軍、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Front General of Security, and General Who Commands the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as attendant-in-ordinary, front general of security, and general who commands the army.

sentences.zh: 十八年，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督荊湘雍梁益寧南北秦八州諸軍事、征西將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant at the Palace Gate, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the eight provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang, Yi, Ning, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, General Who Conquers the West, Commissioner with the Grand Chariot and Three Dignitaries, and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, regular attendant at the palace gate, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the eight provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang, Yi, Ning, southern Qin, and northern Qin, general who conquers the west, commissioner with the grand chariot and three dignitaries, and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 普通五年，進號驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Putong his title was advanced to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Putong his title was advanced to grand general of the flying cavalry.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，薨于州，時年五十一。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year he died in the province, at the age of fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year he died in the province, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「故使持節、散騎常侍、都督荊湘雍梁益寧南北秦八州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史鄱陽王恢，風度開朗，器情凝質。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The late Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant at the Palace Gate, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the eight provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang, Yi, Ning, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, Commissioner with the Grand Chariot and Three Dignitaries, and Governor of Jingzhou, the Prince of Poyang Hui—his bearing was open and bright, his character and disposition firm and pure.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "The late bearer of the staff of authority, regular attendant at the palace gate, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the eight provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang, Yi, Ning, southern Qin, and northern Qin, grand general of the flying cavalry, commissioner with the grand chariot and three dignitaries, and governor of Jingzhou, Prince of Poyang Hui—his bearing was open and bright, his character and disposition firm and pure.

sentences.zh: 爰在弱歲，美譽克宣，洎于從政，嘉猷載緝。

translations.literal: From his tender years fine reputation was fully expressed; upon entering public service excellent plans were continuously gathered.
translations.idiomatic: From his tender years his fine reputation was fully known; upon entering public service excellent plans were continuously gathered.

sentences.zh: 方入正論道，弘燮台階，奄焉薨逝，朕用傷慟于厥心。

translations.literal: Just as he was entering into upright discussion of the Way, to harmonize and assist at the steps of the imperial terrace, suddenly he passed away—We are wounded and grieved in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was entering upright counsel upon the Way, to harmonize and assist at the imperial steps, suddenly he passed away—We are wounded and grieved at heart.

sentences.zh: 宜隆寵命，以申朝典。

translations.literal: It is fitting to elevate his honors so as to fulfill the court's standards.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to elevate his honors in fulfillment of the court's standards.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、司徒，王如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Education, with his princely title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He shall be posthumously granted attendant-in-ordinary and minister of education, with his princely title unchanged.

sentences.zh: 并給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Grant also twenty attendants with ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Grant also twenty attendants with ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠烈。

translations.literal: His posthumous title shall be Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title shall be Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 」遣中書舍人劉顯護喪事。

translations.literal: " The Palace Secretary Attendant Liu Xian was dispatched to oversee the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " The palace secretary attendant Liu Xian was dispatched to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 恢有孝性，初鎮蜀，所生費太妃猶停都，後於都下不豫，恢未之知，一夜忽夢還侍疾，旣覺憂遑，便廢寢食。

translations.literal: Hui had a filial nature; when he first governed Shu his birth mother Consort Fei was still residing in the capital; later she took ill in the capital, though Hui did not know of it. One night he suddenly dreamed of returning to attend her illness; when he awoke he was anxious and distressed and abandoned sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was deeply filial. When he first governed Shu his birth mother, Consort Fei, was still residing in the capital. Later she fell ill in the capital, though Hui did not yet know of it. One night he suddenly dreamed of returning to attend her illness; when he awoke he was anxious and distressed and abandoned sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 俄而都信至，太妃已瘳。

translations.literal: Soon a messenger arrived from the capital and the consort had already recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a messenger arrived from the capital with word that the consort had already recovered.

sentences.zh: 後又目有疾，久廢視瞻，有北渡道人慧龍得治眼術，恢請之。

translations.literal: Later he also had an eye ailment and for a long time ceased to use his sight; there was a monk from north of the river named Huilong who had mastered eye-treatment techniques, and Hui summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also suffered from an eye ailment and for a long time could not see properly. There was a monk from north of the river named Huilong who had mastered eye-treatment techniques, and Hui summoned him.

sentences.zh: 旣至，空中忽見聖僧，及慧龍下針，豁然開朗，咸謂精誠所致。

translations.literal: When he arrived, a holy monk suddenly appeared in midair; when Huilong applied his needles his sight opened clear and bright, and all said it was due to his sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, a holy monk suddenly appeared in midair. When Huilong applied his needles, Hui's sight cleared at once, and all said it was due to his sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 恢性通恕，輕財好施，凡歷四州，所得俸祿隨而散之。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was open and forgiving; he lightly regarded wealth and loved to give. In all the four provinces he served, whatever salary he received he promptly distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was open and forgiving by nature; he lightly regarded wealth and loved to give. In all four provinces he served, he promptly distributed whatever salary he received.

sentences.zh: 在荊州，常從容問賓僚曰：「中山好酒，趙王好吏，二者孰愈？

translations.literal: While in Jingzhou he would calmly ask his guests and aides: "The Prince of Zhongshan loved wine; the Prince of Zhao loved administration—which is better?
translations.idiomatic: While in Jingzhou he would calmly ask his guests and aides: "The Prince of Zhongshan loved wine; the Prince of Zhao loved administration—which is better?

sentences.zh: 」衆未有對者。

translations.literal: " None of the assembly had a reply.
translations.idiomatic: " No one in the assembly had an answer.

sentences.zh: 顧謂長史蕭琛曰：「漢時王侯，籓屏而已，視事親民，自有其職。

translations.literal: He turned and said to his chief of staff Xiao Chen: "In Han times the kings and marquises were merely screen-walls for the realm; governing affairs and caring for the people each had its proper office.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his chief of staff, Xiao Chen, and said: "In Han times the kings and marquises were merely screen-walls for the realm; governing affairs and caring for the people each had its proper office.

sentences.zh: 中山聽樂，可得任性；

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan listening to music—one may follow one's nature;
translations.idiomatic: For the Prince of Zhongshan listening to music, one might follow one's nature;

sentences.zh: 彭祖代吏，近於侵官。

translations.literal: Pengzu acting in place of the clerk approaches overstepping official duty.
translations.idiomatic: for Pengzu acting in place of the clerk, that approaches overstepping official duty.

sentences.zh: 今之王侯，不守籓國，當佐天子臨民，清白其優乎！

translations.literal: Today's kings and marquises do not guard their princely states but ought to assist the Son of Heaven in governing the people—integrity is the better course, is it not!
translations.idiomatic: Today's princes no longer guard their own states but ought to assist the Son of Heaven in governing the people—isn't integrity the better course?

sentences.zh: 」坐賓咸服。

translations.literal: " All the seated guests admired him fully.
translations.idiomatic: " All the guests present admired him.

sentences.zh: 世子範嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Fan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Fan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 範字世儀，溫和有器識。

translations.literal: Fan's style was Shiyi; he was mild and possessed judgment and insight.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, styled Shiyi, was mild-tempered and possessed judgment and insight.

sentences.zh: 起家太子洗馬、秘書郎，歷黃門郎，遷衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He began his career as Groom of the Crown Prince's Household and Secretariat Gentleman, served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and was promoted to Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as groom of the crown prince's household and secretariat gentleman, served as gentleman at the yellow gate, and was promoted to commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 每夜自巡警，高祖嘉其勞苦。

translations.literal: Every night he personally made inspection rounds; the High Ancestor praised his labor and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Every night he personally made inspection rounds, and Emperor Wu praised his diligence.

sentences.zh: 出爲益州刺史，開通劍道，剋復華陽，增邑一千戶，加鼓吹。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Yizhou, opened the Jian Road, recovered Huayang, received an increase of one thousand households to his fief, and was granted martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Yizhou, opened the Jian Road, recovered Huayang, received an increase of one thousand households to his fief, and was granted martial music.

sentences.zh: 徵爲領軍將軍、侍中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General Who Commands the Army and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as general who commands the army and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 範雖無學術，而以籌略自命。

translations.literal: Although Fan had no scholarly learning, he considered himself a strategist by his own account.
translations.idiomatic: Although Fan had no scholarly learning, he considered himself a strategist.

sentences.zh: 愛奇翫古，招集文才，率意題章，亦時有奇致。

translations.literal: He loved the strange and delighted in antiquity, gathered literary talent, composed on impulse, and at times achieved striking effects.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the strange and delighted in antiquity, gathered literary talent, composed on impulse, and at times achieved striking effects.

sentences.zh: 復出爲使持節、都督雍梁東益南北秦五州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Yong, Liang, Eastern Yi, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Yong, Liang, eastern Yi, southern Qin, and northern Qin, general who guards the north, and governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 範作牧蒞民，甚得時譽；

translations.literal: Fan as governor overseeing the people won great contemporary reputation;
translations.idiomatic: As governor overseeing the people, Fan won great contemporary reputation;

sentences.zh: 撫循將士，盡獲歡心。

translations.literal: in comforting and guiding officers and soldiers he fully won their affection.
translations.idiomatic: in comforting and guiding officers and soldiers he fully won their affection.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，大舉北伐，以範爲使持節、征北大將軍、總督漢北征討諸軍事，進伐穰城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing a great northern campaign was launched; Fan was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General Who Conquers the North, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs for Campaigns North of the Han, and advanced to attack Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing a great northern campaign was launched. Fan was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, grand general who conquers the north, and commander-in-chief of all military affairs for campaigns north of the Han, and advanced to attack Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋遷安北將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to general who pacifies the north and governor of southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 侯景敗於渦陽，退保壽陽，乃改範爲合州刺史，鎮合肥。

translations.literal: Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang and withdrew to defend Shouyang; Fan was then changed to Governor of Hezhou and garrisoned Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang and withdrew to defend Shouyang; Fan was then reassigned as governor of Hezhou and garrisoned Hefei.

sentences.zh: 時景已蓄姦謀，不臣將露，範屢啓言之，朱异每抑而不奏。

translations.literal: At that time Jing had already harbored treacherous schemes and his disloyalty was about to be exposed; Fan repeatedly memorialized to report this, but Zhu Yi each time suppressed it without submitting it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hou Jing had already harbored treacherous schemes and his disloyalty was about to show; Fan repeatedly memorialized to warn of this, but Zhu Yi each time suppressed the reports without forwarding them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及景圍京邑，範遣世子嗣與裴之高等入援，遷開府儀同三司，進號征北將軍。

translations.literal: When Jing besieged the capital Fan sent the heir Si and Pei Zhigao and others to enter and reinforce; Fan was promoted to Commissioner with the Grand Chariot and Three Dignitaries and his title was advanced to General Who Conquers the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Fan sent the heir Si and Pei Zhigao and others to reinforce the city. He was promoted to commissioner with the grand chariot and three dignitaries and his title was advanced to general who conquers the north.

sentences.zh: 京城不守，範乃棄合肥，出東關，請兵于魏，遣二子爲質。

translations.literal: When the capital could not be held Fan abandoned Hefei, exited through Dongguan, requested troops from Wei, and sent two sons as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Fan abandoned Hefei, exited through Dongguan, requested troops from Northern Wei, and sent two sons as hostages.

sentences.zh: 魏人據合肥，竟不出師助範，範進退無計，乃沂流西上，軍于樅陽，遣信告尋陽王。

translations.literal: The Wei people occupied Hefei and ultimately did not send troops to aid Fan; Fan had no plan for advance or retreat, so he went upstream westward, encamped at Zongyang, and sent a message to the Prince of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei occupied Hefei and ultimately sent no troops to aid Fan. With no plan for advance or retreat, he went upstream westward, encamped at Zongyang, and sent a message to the Prince of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 尋陽要還九江，欲共治兵西上，范得書大喜，乃引軍至湓城，以晉熙爲晉州，遣子嗣爲刺史。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xunyang wanted to return to Jiujiang and wished to jointly govern troops westward; Fan, receiving the letter, was greatly pleased, then led his army to Pencheng, established Jinxia as Jinzhou, and sent his son Si as governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xunyang wanted to return to Jiujiang and proposed jointly leading troops westward. Fan, receiving the letter, was greatly pleased, then led his army to Pencheng, established Jinxia as Jin Province, and sent his son Si as governor.

sentences.zh: 江州郡縣，輒更改易，尋陽政令所行，惟存一郡，時論以此少之。

translations.literal: In Jiangzhou commanderies and counties he repeatedly changed and replaced officials; of the Prince of Xunyang's government orders only one commandery remained in effect, and contemporary opinion for this thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly changed the officials of Jiangzhou's commanderies and counties; of the Prince of Xunyang's government orders only one commandery remained in effect, and contemporary opinion thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 旣商旅不通，信使距絕，范數萬之衆，皆無復食，人多餓死。

translations.literal: Since merchants and travelers could not pass and messengers were cut off, Fan's force of tens of thousands all had no food left, and many people starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: With merchants and travelers unable to pass and messengers cut off, Fan's force of tens of thousands ran out of food, and many starved to death.

sentences.zh: 範恚，發背薨，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Fan, in fury, developed a carbuncle on his back and died, at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Fan died of rage, from a carbuncle on his back, at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 始興忠武王嶦字僧達，太祖第十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhongwu of Shixing Dan, styled Sengda, was the eleventh son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhongwu of Shixing, Dan, whose style was Sengda, was the founding emperor's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 數歲，所生母吳太妃卒，嶦哀感傍人。

translations.literal: At several years of age his birth mother Consort Wu died; Dan's grief moved those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was only a few years old his birth mother, Consort Wu, died. Dan's grief moved all who witnessed it.

sentences.zh: 齊世，弱冠爲西中郎法曹行參軍，遷外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Under Qi, at his capping he became Acting Army Aide of the Legal Bureau under the Western Central Commandant and was transferred to Army Aide of the Outer Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi, upon reaching his capping age he served as acting aide in the legal bureau under the western central commandant, and was later transferred to aide in the outer bureau.

sentences.zh: 義師起，南康王承制，以嶦爲冠軍將軍、西中郎諮議參軍，遷相國從事中郎，與南平王偉留守。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, the Prince of Nankang assumed the regency and made Dan General of the Champion Army and Advisory Army Aide under the Western Central Commandant; he was transferred to Aide of the Affairs Bureau under the Chancellor of State and remained with the Prince of Nanping Wei to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Prince Nankang assumed the regency and appointed Dan general of the champion army and advisory aide under the western central commandant. He was promoted to aide of the chancellor's affairs bureau and remained with Prince Nanping, Wei, to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 和帝立，以嶦爲給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor He was enthroned, Dan was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He was enthroned, Dan was appointed attendant gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 時巴東太守蕭慧訓子璝等及巴西太守魯休烈舉兵逼荊州，屯軍上明，鎮軍將軍蕭穎胄暴疾卒，西朝甚懼，尚書僕射夏侯祥議徵兵雍州，南平王偉遣嶦赴之。

translations.literal: At that time the son of the Governor of Badong Xiao Huixun, Gui, and the Governor of Baxi Lu Xiulie raised troops to press Jing Province and encamped at Shangming; the Stabilizing Army General Xiao Yingzhou died suddenly of illness, and the western court was greatly afraid; Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xiahou Xiang proposed recruiting troops from Yong Province, and the Prince of Nanping Wei sent Dan to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gui, son of the governor of Badong, Xiao Huixun, and the governor of Baxi, Lu Xiulie, raised troops against Jing Province and encamped at Shangming. Stabilizing Army General Xiao Yingzhou died suddenly, and the western court was seized with fear. Vice Director Xiahou Xiang proposed recruiting troops from Yong Province, and Prince Nanping, Wei, sent Dan to their aid.

sentences.zh: 嶦以書喻璝等，旬日皆請降。

translations.literal: Dan wrote letters to instruct Gui and the others, and within ten days all asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dan wrote letters persuading Gui and the others, and within ten days all asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 是冬，高祖平建業。

translations.literal: That winter the High Ancestor pacified Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Wu pacified Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 明年春，和帝將發江陵，詔以嶦爲使持節、都督荊湘益寧南北秦六州諸軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史，未拜。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year, as Emperor He was about to depart from Jiangling, an edict made Dan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the six provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yi, Ning, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Jing Province, but he did not take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the following year, as Emperor He was about to depart from Jiangling, an edict appointed Dan bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Jing, Xiang, Yi, Ning, southern Qin, and northern Qin, general who pacifies the west, and governor of Jing Province, but he did not yet assume the post.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，加安西將軍，都督、刺史如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the West; his posts as Commander-in-Chief and Governor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he was additionally appointed general who pacifies the west, while his posts as commander and governor remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 封始興郡王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Prince of Shixing with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅之後，公私空乏，嶦厲精爲治，廣辟屯田，減省力役，存問兵死之家，供其窮困，民甚安之。

translations.literal: At that time, in the aftermath of military campaigns, public and private resources were exhausted; Dan devoted himself energetically to governance, broadly opened military colonies, reduced and lightened corvée labor, inquired after families of soldiers who had died, supplied their destitution, and the people were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, in the aftermath of war, public and private resources were exhausted. Dan devoted himself energetically to governance, broadly opened military colonies, reduced corvée labor, inquired after families of fallen soldiers, and supplied their needs. The people were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 嶦自以少年始居重任，思欲開導物情。

translations.literal: Dan considered that from youth he had first held a weighty post and wished to open and guide popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Dan felt that from youth he had borne heavy responsibility and wished to open channels for popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 乃謂佐吏曰：「政之不臧，士君子所宜共惜。

translations.literal: He therefore said to his staff officers: "When government is not good, gentlemen ought together to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told his staff, "When government goes wrong, gentlemen ought together to regret it.

sentences.zh: 言可用，用之可也；

translations.literal: If words can be used, use them;
translations.idiomatic: If advice can be used, use it;

sentences.zh: 如不用，於我何傷？

translations.literal: if not used, what harm to me?
translations.idiomatic: if not, what harm does it do me?

sentences.zh: 吾開懷矣，爾其無吝。

translations.literal: I have opened my heart—do not be sparing."
translations.idiomatic: I have opened my heart to you—do not hold back."

sentences.zh: 」於是小人知恩，而君子盡意。

translations.literal: " Thereupon petty men knew gratitude and gentlemen gave their full counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon petty men knew gratitude, and gentlemen gave their full counsel.

sentences.zh: 民辭訟者，皆立前待符教，決於俄頃。

translations.literal: When the people came to plead lawsuits, all stood before him awaiting his written orders and were decided in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: When the people came to plead lawsuits, all stood before him awaiting his written orders, and cases were decided in an instant.

sentences.zh: 曹無留事，下無滯獄，民益悅焉。

translations.literal: The offices had no backlog of business, below there were no delayed cases in prison, and the people were increasingly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The offices had no backlog of business, and no cases languished in prison. The people were increasingly pleased.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict added a set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict granted him an additional set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 六年，州大水，江溢堤壞，嶦親率府將吏，冒雨賦丈尺築治之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the province suffered great flood; the river overflowed and the dikes broke; Dan personally led the prefectural generals and officials, braving rain to measure out dimensions and build repairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the province suffered a great flood. The river overflowed and the dikes broke. Dan personally led the prefectural generals and officials, braving rain to measure and repair the dikes.

sentences.zh: 雨甚水壯，衆皆恐，或請嶦避焉。

translations.literal: The rain was heavy and the waters mighty; all were afraid, and some asked Dan to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The rain was heavy and the waters rose fiercely. All were afraid, and some asked Dan to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 嶦曰：「王尊尚欲身塞河堤，我獨何心以免。

translations.literal: Dan said: "Wang Zun was still willing to block the river dikes with his own body—how could I alone wish to escape."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Wang Zun was willing to block the river dikes with his own body—how could I alone wish to escape."

sentences.zh: 」乃刑白馬祭江神。

translations.literal: " He then executed a white horse as sacrifice to the river god.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sacrificed a white horse to the river god.

sentences.zh: 俄而水退堤立。

translations.literal: Soon the waters receded and the dikes stood firm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the waters receded and the dikes stood firm.

sentences.zh: 邴州在南岸，數百家見水長驚走，登屋緣樹，憺募人救之，一口賞一萬，估客數十人應募救焉，州民乃以免。

translations.literal: Bing Province was on the south bank; several hundred households, seeing the waters rise, fled in alarm, climbing onto roofs and into trees; Dan recruited men to rescue them, offering ten thousand per person saved; several dozen merchant travelers answered the call and rescued them, and the people of the province were thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: On the south bank several hundred households, seeing the waters rise, fled in alarm and climbed onto roofs and into trees. Dan recruited rescuers, offering ten thousand cash per person saved. Several dozen merchant travelers answered the call, and the people of the province were spared.

sentences.zh: 又分遣行諸郡，遭水死者給棺槥，失田者與糧種。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys separately through the commanderies: those who died in the flood were given coffins; those who lost fields were given grain seed.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys through the commanderies: those who died in the flood were given coffins, and those who lost their fields were given grain seed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，嘉禾生於州界，吏民歸美，嶦謙讓不受。

translations.literal: That year auspicious grain grew within the province's borders; officials and people attributed the blessing to him, but Dan modestly declined to accept the credit.
translations.idiomatic: That year auspicious grain appeared within the province. Officials and people attributed the blessing to him, but Dan modestly declined the credit.

sentences.zh: 七年，慈母陳太妃薨，水漿不入口六日，居喪過禮，高祖優詔勉之，使攝州任。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his beloved mother Consort Chen died; he took no water or gruel for six days and observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites; the High Ancestor sent a gracious edict to encourage him and ordered him to act in the governor's place.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his beloved foster mother, Consort Chen, died. He took no food or drink for six days and observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites. Emperor Wu sent a gracious edict encouraging him and ordered him to resume provincial duties.

sentences.zh: 是冬，詔徵以本號還朝。

translations.literal: That winter an edict summoned him back to court with his existing title.
translations.idiomatic: That winter an edict summoned him back to court with his existing title.

sentences.zh: 民爲之歌曰：「始興王，民之爹。

translations.literal: The people made a song saying: "The Prince of Shixing is the people's father.
translations.idiomatic: The people composed a song: "Prince of Shixing is the people's father.

sentences.zh: 赴人急，如水火。

translations.literal: He rushes to men's urgency like water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: He rushes to help the needy as water and fire rush together.

sentences.zh: 何時復來哺乳我？

translations.literal: When will he come again to nurse and feed us?"
translations.idiomatic: When will he come again to nurture us?"

sentences.zh: 」八年，爲平北將軍、護軍將軍、領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: " In the eighth year he became General Who Pacifies the North, Protector of the Army, and overseer of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth year he was appointed general who pacifies the north, protector of the army, and overseer of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中軍將軍、中書令，俄領衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General of the Central Army and Director of the Secretariat, and shortly thereafter concurrently served as Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to general of the central army and director of the secretariat, and shortly thereafter concurrently served as commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 嶦性勞謙，降意接士，常與賓客連榻而坐，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Dan's nature was industrious and modest; he lowered himself to receive gentlemen and often sat on connected couches with his guests—contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was industrious and modest by nature. He lowered himself to receive gentlemen and often sat on connected couches with his guests, which contemporaries praised.

sentences.zh: 是秋，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督南北兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: That autumn he went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Southern and Northern Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was posted as bearer of the staff of authority, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, commander of military affairs in southern and northern Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, general who pacifies the north, and governor of southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 九年春，遷都督益寧南梁南北秦沙六州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the six provinces of Yi, Ning, Southern Liang, Southern Qin, Northern Qin, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he was transferred to commander of military affairs in Yi, Ning, southern Liang, southern Qin, northern Qin, and Sha, general who pacifies the west, and governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 開立學校，勸課就業，遣子映親受經焉，由是多向方者。

translations.literal: He established schools, encouraged instruction and employment, and sent his son Ying to receive the classics in person—thereby many turned toward the right path.
translations.idiomatic: He established schools, encouraged instruction, and sent his son Ying to study the classics in person. Many thereby turned toward learning.

sentences.zh: 時魏襲巴南，西圍南安，南安太守垣季珪堅壁固守，嶦遣軍救之，魏人退走，所收器械甚衆。

translations.literal: At that time Wei raided southern Ba and besieged Nan'an from the west; the Governor of Nan'an Yuan Jigui held firm behind his walls; Dan sent troops to relieve him, the Wei forces withdrew, and the weapons captured were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Northern Wei raided southern Ba and besieged Nan'an from the west. The governor of Nan'an, Yuan Jigui, held firm behind his walls. Dan sent troops to relieve him; the Wei forces withdrew, and a great quantity of weapons was captured.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷都督荊湘雍寧南梁南北秦七州諸軍事、鎮右將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the seven provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Ning, Southern Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin, General Who Pacifies the Right, and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to commander of military affairs in Jing, Xiang, Yong, Ning, southern Liang, southern Qin, and northern Qin, general who pacifies the right, and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 同母兄安成王秀將之雍州，薨於道。

translations.literal: His uterine elder brother the Prince of Ancheng Xiu was proceeding to Yong Province and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: His uterine elder brother Prince Ancheng, Xiu, was proceeding to Yong Province and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 嶦聞喪，自投于地，席稾稿哭泣，不飲不食者數日，傾財產賻送，部伍小大皆取足焉。

translations.literal: When Dan heard of the mourning he threw himself to the ground, lay on straw matting and wailed, and for several days took neither drink nor food; he exhausted his property for funeral gifts, and every member of the entourage, high and low, was fully provided for.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan heard of his death he threw himself to the ground, lay on straw matting and wailed, and for several days took neither food nor drink. He exhausted his property for funeral gifts, and every member of the entourage, high and low, was fully provided for.

sentences.zh: 天下稱其悌。

translations.literal: All under Heaven praised his fraternal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven praised his fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 十八年，徵爲侍中、中撫將軍、開府儀同三司、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant, Central Pacifying General, with ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies and an open office, and Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was summoned as palace attendant, central pacifying general, with the ceremonial privileges of the three excellencies and an open office, and commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 普通三年十一月，薨，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Putong he died, at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Putong he died, at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、司徒、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, and Grand General of the Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of palace attendant, minister of education, and grand general of the flying cavalry.

sentences.zh: 給班劍三十人，羽葆鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was given thirty ceremonial sword guards and a set of feathered parasols and martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted thirty ceremonial sword guards and a set of feathered parasols and martial music.

sentences.zh: 册曰：「咨故侍中、司徒、驃騎將軍始興王：夫忠爲令德，武謂止戈，于以用之，載在前志。

translations.literal: The patent of enfeoffment said: "We consult the late Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, Prince of Shixing: loyalty is the foremost virtue, martial prowess means halting warfare—these are applied as recorded in former chronicles.
translations.idiomatic: The patent of enfeoffment declared: "We address the late palace attendant, minister of education, and grand general of the flying cavalry, Prince of Shixing: loyalty is the foremost virtue, and martial prowess means halting warfare—these principles are recorded in former chronicles.

sentences.zh: 王有佐命之元勳，利民之厚德，契闊二紀，始終不渝，是用方軌往賢，稽擇故訓，鴻名美義，允臻其極。

translations.literal: The prince had the supreme merit of assisting in the founding mandate and the deep virtue of benefiting the people; through two decades of trials his constancy never wavered—therefore We align him with sages of old, examine and select former teachings, and his great name and fine meaning reach their utmost limit.
translations.idiomatic: The prince possessed the supreme merit of assisting in the founding of the dynasty and the deep virtue of benefiting the people. Through two decades of trials his constancy never wavered. We therefore align him with sages of old, examine former teachings, and grant him a great name and fine meaning reaching their utmost limit.

sentences.zh: 今遣兼大鴻臚程爽，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Now We send the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies Cheng Shuang; his posthumous title shall be Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: We now send Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies Cheng Shuang to confer the posthumous title Zhongwu, "Loyal and Martial."

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，歆茲顯號。

translations.literal: If your soul has awareness, receive this illustrious title.
translations.idiomatic: If your soul has awareness, receive this illustrious title.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！」

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!"

sentences.zh: 嶦未薨前，夢改封中山王，策授如他日，意頗惡之，數旬而卒。

translations.literal: Before Dan died he dreamed that his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Zhongshan, with investiture as on other days; he was rather ill at ease about it, and within several tens of days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before his death Dan dreamed that his title was changed to Prince of Zhongshan, with investiture conducted as on other occasions. He was troubled by the dream, and within several weeks he died.

sentences.zh: 世子亮嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Liang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent, Liang, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自昔王者創業，廣植親親，割裂州國，封建子弟。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From of old when kings founded their enterprises, they broadly planted kinship, carved up provinces and states, and enfeoffed sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: From of old, when kings founded their enterprises, they broadly cultivated kinship, carved up provinces and states, and enfeoffed sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 是以大旂少帛，崇於魯、衛，磐石凝脂，樹斯梁、楚。

translations.literal: Therefore the great banners and lesser silks were honored in Lu and Wei, and the bedrock congealed like fat was planted in Liang and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the great banners and lesser silks were honored in Lu and Wei, and bedrock solid as congealed fat was planted in Liang and Chu.

sentences.zh: 高祖遠遵前軌，籓屏懿親。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor followed the distant former track and made his fine kinsmen screens for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu followed this distant precedent and made his fine kinsmen screens for the realm.

sentences.zh: 至於安成、南平，鄱陽、始興，俱以名跡著，蓋亦漢之間、平矣。

translations.literal: As for Ancheng, Nanping, Poyang, and Shixing—all were renowned for name and achievement; they were perhaps the Jian and Ping of Han.
translations.idiomatic: As for Ancheng, Nanping, Poyang, and Shixing—all were renowned for name and achievement. They were perhaps the Jian and Ping of Han.

translations.idiomatic: Note 1.
